correctness.rationale: For Laplacian edge weights (1,t,t,1), t>0, use C=2R−I and reflection decomposition into even 3x3/odd 2x2 blocks. Independently checked with symbolic inversion D1=h²t+2ht+4h+4, D2=5h²t+6ht+4h+4, central return D1/D2, shoulder (h+2)[(1+ht)/D2+1/D1], and the signed shoulder−center expression. Exact substitution at h=2,t=3/4 yields zero CN diagonal entries at the three inner sites and positive outer ones. Off-diagonals are strictly positive by irreducible M-matrix inversion. Every resolvent return decreases continuously from 1 to 1/5 and crosses 1/2 once. At center crossing the difference sign factors through h−2, giving the unique switch t=3/4; implicit polynomial scaling supports H_f(t)=2/sqrt(t)−sqrt(t)+O(t). Proof also compares symmetric paths of sizes 3,4; t=0 is handled separately.

originality.rationale: The published reversible-Markov return law already establishes C=2R-I, diagonal half threshold and monotone return probabilities; the published uniform reflecting-path theorem covers only equal conductances, with a central obstruction. Neither source evaluates the 1,t,t,1 path across t, finds the shoulder-to-center switch at 3/4 or the singular weak-coupling scaling. Published other Crank–Nicolson studies concern different operators or graph structures. Best-of-knowledge originality for the structural active-site switch.
residual_risks: Older nonuniform Stieltjes-resolvent or heat-scheme paper might already contain this explicit five-node crossing under different notation.
Finite symbolic/numeric checks do not replace the analytic all-parameter crossing argument; no independent expert attestation is asserted.

value.rationale: A counterintuitive switch of which physical site first loses positivity, with an exact conductance boundary and divergent weak-coupling safe-step law, is a useful nonuniform-grid structural benchmark. Its five-site minimality distinguishes genuine heterogeneity from routine explicit evaluation of a general implicit eigenvalue criterion.

limitations: Best-of-knowledge literature coverage is not a universal novelty proof. Finite computations corroborate but do not replace analytically quantified proof steps; see separate C/O/V evidence.
